definitions.explanation: A paved path for pedestrians alongside a road.

examples.japanese: {歩道|ほどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いて→あるく：00538_aruku⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
{歩道|ほどう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→じてんしゃ：00633_jitensha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まっている→とまる：00555_tomaru⟧。
examples.english: A bicycle is parked on the sidewalk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歩道橋|ほどうきょう}→ほどうきょう：06494_hodoukyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}って→わたる：02441_wataru⟧⟦{反対側|はんたいがわ}→はんたいがわ：16780_hantaigawa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→いく：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I'll cross using the pedestrian overpass to get to the other side.

notes:
A paved path for pedestrians running alongside a road. Composed of {歩|ほ} (walk) + {道|どう} (road, path).

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{歩道橋|ほどうきょう}→ほどうきょう：06494_hodoukyou⟧: pedestrian overpass
- ⟦{横断歩道|おうだんほどう}→おうだんほどう：06502_oudanhodou⟧: crosswalk, pedestrian crossing
- ⟦{遊歩道|ゆうほどう}→ゆうほどう：23484_yuuhodou⟧: promenade, walking path

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{車道|しゃどう}→しゃどう：03066_shadou⟧: roadway for vehicles
- ⟦{道路|どうろ}→どうろ：01481_douro⟧: road (general)
- ⟦{通路|つうろ}→つうろ：04062_tsuuro⟧: passage, walkway (indoor)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, bicycles are often legally permitted on sidewalks (especially wide ones or when marked), unlike in many Western countries. Signs indicating ⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→じてんしゃ：00633_jitensha⟧⟦{通行|つうこう}→つうこう：03436_tsuukou⟧⟦{可|か}→か：noentry⟧ mark sidewalks where cycling is allowed.
